title: 2025 Supervisory Stress Test Methodology
summary: The Federal Reserve published its 2025 Supervisory Stress Test Methodology document in June 2025, detailing the models used to assess how large banks ($100B+ in assets) would perform under hypothetical severe economic conditions. The methodology covers models for projecting pre-tax net income, loan losses across corporate, commercial real estate, residential mortgage, and credit card portfolios, and the calculation of regulatory capital ratios. The stress test cycle produces four key publications annually: scenarios, methodology, results, and capital requirements.
key_points: Banks with $100B+ in assets are subject to supervisory stress tests under Dodd-Frank Act requirements (12 C.F.R. pt. 238, subpt. O; pt. 252, subpt. E)
The stress test cycle publishes four documents: Stress Test Scenarios (mid-February), Methodology, Results (end of Q2), and Large Bank Capital Requirements (Q3)
Supervisory models project losses, revenues, expenses, and resulting capital levels under hypothetical economic conditions
Model categories include: Pre-provision Net Revenue, Loan Losses (corporate, CRE, first-lien residential mortgage, credit card), Other Losses, and Regulatory Capital Ratios
Loan loss models are category-specific: Corporate Loan Model, Commercial Real Estate Loan Model, Domestic First-Lien Residential Mortgage Model, and Domestic Credit Card Model
Stress test results inform capital requirements for participating banks and assess whether banks are sufficiently capitalized to absorb losses during a severe recession
The document includes Appendix A (model changes for 2025), Appendix B (result templates), and Appendix C (loan category definitions)
why_it_matters: This methodology document is the technical foundation for understanding how the Federal Reserve evaluates bank resilience. For market participants, the stress test results (published end of Q2) directly affect capital requirements and can influence bank lending capacity, dividend/share buyback decisions, and risk appetite. The methodology reveals which loan categories and economic variables the Fed considers most sensitive in stress scenarios, providing insight into supervisory priorities.
macro_context: The stress test methodology itself does not contain macroeconomic projections; those are published separately in the Stress Test Scenarios document (typically mid-February). This methodology document describes the modeling framework applied to whatever economic scenarios are specified.
market_structure_context: While not directly addressing market microstructure (trading venues, order flow, market making), this methodology shapes bank behavior in capital markets through capital requirements. The balance sheet projections and regulatory capital ratio calculations determine how much capital banks must hold against various asset classes, influencing their market participation and risk management practices.
